title: Use trusted identity propagation for Apache Spark interactive sessions in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Interactive Spark sessions in SageMaker Unified Studio on EMR, EMR Serverless and Glue 5.0 can now run as the signed-in Identity Center user instead of the shared project role.
Lake Formation tag-based grants to Identity Center groups then decide per user which columns are visible, and CloudTrail records the real user.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Lake Formation, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon EMR Serverless
decision: Per-user identity propagation vs project IAM roles for Spark data access in SageMaker Unified Studio
authors: Aarthi Srinivasan, Palani Nagarajan

title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports 10x larger record sizes: Simplifying real-time data processing
key_points: AWS reports Kinesis Data Streams now accepts records up to 10 MiB (from 1 MiB), set per stream, with the same producer and consumer APIs, which removes the need to split records or pass S3 pointers for occasional large payloads.

Per-shard throughput limits do not change: a shard can burst for a large record and then refills, so throttling grows as large records become more frequent; AWS reports best results when they stay around 1-2% of records.
Check every consumer first; AWS lists KCL 2.x, Firehose to S3 and Lambda as able to handle large records.
services: Amazon Kinesis, Kinesis Data Streams, AWS Lambda, Amazon Data Firehose
decision: Large Kinesis records vs splitting records vs S3 pointer (claim check) for occasional oversized payloads
authors: Sumant Nemmani, Umesh Chaudhari, Pratik Patel

title: Federate access to SageMaker Unified Studio with AWS IAM Identity Center and Okta
key_points: Step-by-step setup of Okta as the identity provider for IAM Identity Center using SAML and SCIM user sync, then single sign-on into SageMaker Unified Studio.
Identity administration rather than data work.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, Okta
authors: Raghavarao Sodabathina, Jacob Grant, Nicholaus Lawson, Matt Nispel

title: Implement fine-grained access control for Iceberg tables using Amazon EMR on EKS integrated with AWS Lake Formation
key_points: Lake Formation now enforces row, column and cell filters on Spark jobs running on EMR on EKS, so different teams' jobs see different slices of the same Iceberg tables.
Cross-account data-mesh setup: the producer account owns the tables and filters, the consumer account maps EKS namespaces and job roles to teams and runs PySpark jobs that return only permitted data.
Ends with the current limitations of the feature.
services: Amazon EMR on EKS, AWS Lake Formation, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon EKS
decision: Lake Formation fine-grained filters enforced in Spark vs separate filtered copies per team for cross-account Iceberg data sharing
authors: Tejal Patel, Janakiraman Shanmugam, Prabhakaran Thatchinamoorthy

title: Accelerate data governance with custom subscription workflows in Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Low-sensitivity assets in SageMaker can be approved automatically, either per asset or through a custom workflow.
An EventBridge rule on subscription requests calls a Lambda function that approves or routes the request and notifies through SNS.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS
authors: Nira Jaiswal, Ajit Tandale

title: Unlock real-time data insights with schema evolution using Amazon MSK Serverless, Iceberg, and AWS Glue streaming
key_points: End-to-end CDC build: Debezium on MSK Connect reads MySQL changes into MSK Serverless, a Glue streaming job applies inserts, updates and deletes to an Iceberg table, and Athena queries it.

Schema evolution is partly automated: each micro-batch is compared with the catalog schema and new columns are added with ALTER TABLE, while dropped, renamed or retyped columns still need manual work.
Everything is deployed with one CloudFormation template, which makes it easy to reproduce.
services: AWS Glue, Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Connect, Debezium, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena, Amazon RDS for MySQL
decision: Glue streaming vs Firehose vs Flink for applying CDC with schema changes to Iceberg tables
attaches_to: aws-bytes: change data capture (DMS vs zero-ETL) / real-time streaming (later)
authors: Nitin Kumar, Shubham Purwar, Noritaka Sekiyama

title: Upgrade from Amazon Redshift DC2 node type to Amazon Redshift Serverless
key_points: Gives AWS's starting RPU sizes for each DC2 cluster size and advises checking them with Redshift Test Drive before cutting over.
The move is a snapshot restore into a Serverless namespace from the console or CLI; interleaved sort keys become compound keys and the endpoint changes, so a CNAME helps.
After the move: close open transactions (they keep consuming RPUs), switch to the unified system views and watch cost before tuning base capacity.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Serverless, Redshift Test Drive
decision: Redshift Serverless vs provisioned (RA3/RG) as the target when retiring DC2 clusters
authors: Nita Shah, Bryan Cottle, Semir Naffati, Ricardo Serafim

title: Stifel’s approach to scalable Data Pipeline Orchestration in Data Mesh
key_points: Stifel triggers domain pipelines when their upstream data products are refreshed, instead of on fixed schedules: producers publish refresh events to a central EventBridge bus that forwards them to each domain account.

Dependencies, schedules and Glue job settings live as metadata in Aurora; Lambda marks each dependency as arrived, Step Functions starts the Glue job once all have arrived, and Glue state-change events update status and publish the next event.
A periodic monitor restarts stuck pipelines and sends failures to a notification queue.
services: Amazon EventBridge, AWS Glue, AWS Lambda, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Aurora, Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS
decision: Event-driven, metadata-defined dependency orchestration vs time-based schedules vs Airflow/MWAA for cross-domain pipelines
authors: Stifel — Srinivas Kandi, Hossein Johari, Ahmad Rawashdeh, Lei Meng, Amit Maindola

title: How Twilio built a multi-engine query platform using Amazon Athena and open-source Presto
key_points: Part 1 of Twilio's series: a gateway called Odin sits in front of Athena and self-managed Presto, so users keep one JDBC endpoint while the platform decides which engine and Athena workgroup runs each query.

Routing uses a user hint plus identity and queue depth, falling back from reserved-capacity workgroups to on-demand ones; Redis tracks running queries and DynamoDB keeps query history so the gateway stays stateless.
Lessons learned cover small result differences between Presto and Athena, such as header rows on paged results and every value coming back as text through the API.
services: Amazon Athena, Athena provisioned capacity, Presto, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon ElastiCache, Amazon EventBridge
decision: Single self-managed engine vs gateway routing across Athena on-demand, Athena provisioned capacity and Presto for a shared query platform
authors: Twilio — Amber Runnels, Aakash Pradeep, Venkatram Bondugula

title: Automate email notifications for governance teams working with Amazon SageMaker Catalog
key_points: EventBridge rules catch SageMaker Catalog events such as new projects and published assets, queue them in SQS and a Lambda function emails the governance team through SNS.
Standard event-to-notification wiring deployed with CDK; nothing specific to data engineering.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon DataZone, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS
authors: Himanshu Sahni, Jitesh Kumar, Rajiv Upadhyay

title: Configure seamless single sign-on with SQL analytics in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: SageMaker Unified Studio can pass the signed-in user's identity (trusted identity propagation) to Redshift and Athena, so Lake Formation rules apply per person rather than per project role.
Walkthrough registers a Redshift cluster in the catalog, grants Lake Formation permissions to Identity Center users and checks two users' different views of S3 and Redshift tables.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena
decision: User identity propagation vs shared project IAM roles for SQL access in SageMaker Unified Studio
authors: Arun A K, Maneesh Sharma, Srividya Parthasarathy

title: Stream mainframe data to AWS in near real time with Precisely and Amazon MSK
key_points: Precisely's replication product captures Db2 changes on z/OS, handles EBCDIC and COMP conversion, and publishes them to an MSK Serverless topic.
MSK Connect with a JDBC sink connector writes the changes into Aurora PostgreSQL; most of the post is setup steps for the partner AMI.
Relevant mainly as a pattern for mainframe CDC in modernisation projects.
services: Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Connect, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS Mainframe Modernization, Precisely
decision: Partner log-based mainframe CDC via Kafka vs batch file extracts for moving mainframe data to AWS
authors: Precisely — Supreet Padhi, Tamara Astakhova, Manasa Ramesh

title: Best practices for upgrading from Amazon Redshift DC2 to RA3 and Amazon Redshift Serverless
key_points: Compares the three upgrade routes off DC2 (snapshot restore, classic resize, elastic resize) on downtime, read-only windows, endpoint changes and data sync effort.
Recommends a phased move: first a like-for-like upgrade checked with Redshift Test Drive, then modernisation with data sharing, zero-ETL and separate Serverless endpoints per workload.
Now that Graviton-based RG instances exist, RA3 is no longer the obvious provisioned target, so this is mainly background on the resize mechanics.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Serverless, Redshift RA3, Redshift Test Drive
decision: Snapshot restore vs classic resize vs elastic resize, and full re-architecture vs phased upgrade, when leaving DC2
authors: Ziad Wali, Omama Khurshid, Srikant Das

title: Visualize data lineage using Amazon SageMaker Catalog for Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Redshift
key_points: SageMaker Catalog accepts OpenLineage events and draws versioned lineage graphs across Glue jobs, Glue notebooks, Redshift queries and EMR Serverless Spark jobs.
The walkthrough loads data from RDS MySQL and shows the job settings each engine needs to emit lineage, and how the graphs appear in the catalog.
Lineage only covers what the engines report, so the setup has to be done per job type.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, Amazon EMR Serverless, OpenLineage
decision: Built-in catalog lineage from Glue/Redshift vs OpenLineage emitted from dbt/Airflow vs no lineage for pipeline governance
authors: Shubham Purwar, Nitin Kumar, Prashanthi Chinthala

title: Building a real-time ICU patient analytics pipeline with AWS Lambda event source mapping
key_points: Sensor readings flow through IoT Core into a Kinesis stream that two Lambda functions read: one uses event-source-mapping filters so it only fires on critical readings, the other keeps state across a tumbling window to build aggregates.
Aggregates go through Firehose into an Iceberg table queried by Athena; DynamoDB stores the last alert time so the same condition does not trigger repeated alerts.
Shows that simple windowed aggregation and filtering on Kinesis can stay in Lambda without a stream-processing engine.
services: Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, AWS IoT Core, Amazon Data Firehose, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon SNS
decision: Lambda event-source-mapping filters and tumbling windows vs Managed Flink for light stream filtering and aggregation on Kinesis
authors: Priyanka Chaudhary, Nihar Sheth, Pratik Patel

title: Breaking down data silos: Volkswagen’s approach with Amazon DataZone
key_points: Volkswagen's production platform had data in separate Redshift warehouses per use case and account, with discovery and access requests handled by hand.
A central DataZone (now SageMaker Catalog) account plus automation in each producer account registers and publishes Redshift tables as catalog assets so other plants can find and request them.
Useful as a data-mesh example where data stays in place and only the catalog is shared.
services: Amazon DataZone, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon Redshift, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge
decision: Central catalog over in-place Redshift warehouses vs consolidating into one warehouse for cross-domain data discovery
authors: Volkswagen — Bandana Das, Anirban Saha, Sindi Cali, Stoyan Stoyanov

title: Best practices for migrating from Apache Airflow 2.x to Apache Airflow 3.x on Amazon MWAA
key_points: Moving MWAA from Airflow 2 to 3 needs a new environment, not an in-place upgrade, because of breaking changes: workers lose direct metadata database access, SubDAGs are gone and scheduling defaults change.
Recommends an inventory of DAGs, plugins and dependencies first, then phased or blue/green cutover, with metadata migration and post-cutover checks.
services: Amazon MWAA, Apache Airflow
decision: Phased vs blue/green migration of Airflow 2 DAGs to a new Airflow 3 MWAA environment
authors: Anurag Srivastava, Ankit Sahu, Kamen Sharlandjiev, Mike Ellis, Jeetendra Vaidya, Venu Thangalapally

title: Seamlessly Integrate Data on Google BigQuery and ClickHouse Cloud with AWS Glue
key_points: A Glue job reads a BigQuery table through Glue's BigQuery connection and writes it to ClickHouse Cloud with the ClickHouse JDBC driver from the Marketplace connector.
Mostly console clicks and one short PySpark script; validation and incremental loads are only mentioned, not shown.
services: AWS Glue, Google BigQuery, ClickHouse Cloud, AWS Secrets Manager
authors: ClickHouse — Ray Wang, Stanley Chukwuemeke, Robert Chung, Tomohiro Tanaka

title: Bridging data silos: cross-bounded context querying with Vanguard’s Operational Read-only Data Store (ORDS) using Amazon Redshift
key_points: Vanguard replaced cross-domain joins on a shared mainframe Db2 with a read-only Redshift store: each domain keeps its own Aurora PostgreSQL or DynamoDB database and publishes read-only views through Redshift data sharing.
Ingestion mixes zero-ETL, DMS from Aurora PostgreSQL, and DynamoDB changes streamed through Kinesis into materialized views, with extra pipelines where compliance needs every transaction replicated.
Includes a short comparison against bulk APIs, a data lake and S3 file exchange, saying when each one fits better.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift data sharing, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS DMS, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Kinesis, Zero-ETL
decision: Redshift read-only store with data sharing vs bulk APIs vs data lake vs S3 file exchange for cross-domain batch reads after breaking up a central database
attaches_to: aws-bytes: change data capture (DMS vs zero-ETL), data sharing (later)
authors: Vanguard — Naresh Rajaram, Malav Shah, Priyadharshini Selvaraj, Timothy Dickens

title: Optimize efficiency with language analyzers using scalable multilingual search in Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: An ML inference processor in the OpenSearch ingest pipeline calls a language-detection model hosted in SageMaker and tags each document's language as it is indexed.
The tag routes text into language-specific analyzers, replacing client-side detection and per-language fields; search relevance work, not data engineering.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon SageMaker
authors: Sunil Ramachandra, Mingshi Liu, Sampath Kathirvel

title: Introducing Apache Airflow 3 on Amazon MWAA: New features and capabilities
key_points: Launch of Airflow 3 on MWAA: a new UI, a Task API so tasks no longer touch the metadata database directly, backfills run by the scheduler instead of the CLI, DAG versioning and a newer Python.
Scheduling becomes event-driven: asset watchers can start DAGs from outside events such as SQS messages, not only from schedules or upstream datasets.
Lists features MWAA does not yet support; the later Airflow 2-to-3 migration guide and the MWAA agent-skills post cover the actual upgrade, so this is background only.
services: Amazon MWAA, Apache Airflow
decision: Event-driven asset triggers vs time-based schedules for starting data pipelines in Airflow
authors: Anurag Srivastava, Ankit Sahu, Kamen Sharlandjiev, Sriharsh Adari, Mohammad Sabeel, Satya Chikkala

title: How Laravel Nightwatch handles billions of observability events in real time with Amazon MSK and ClickHouse Cloud
key_points: Laravel's monitoring product receives telemetry through API Gateway, validates it in Lambda, publishes to MSK Express brokers, and lets ClickHouse Cloud pull the topics directly with its ClickPipes integration, so there is no ETL layer of its own.
Transactional data (accounts, billing) stays in RDS PostgreSQL while analytical events go to ClickHouse, where materialized views shape the raw JSON for sub-second dashboards.
AWS reports load tests above 1 million events per second and about 500 million events processed on launch day; the post is light on design trade-offs and reads mostly as a partner success story.
services: Amazon MSK, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, ClickHouse Cloud
decision: Kafka pulled directly by a real-time OLAP store vs streaming ingestion into a warehouse for high-volume event dashboards
authors: Laravel — Masudur Rahaman Sayem, James Carpenter, Jess Archer, Johnny Mirza
